land.text: present-day County Clare as well as parts of County Limerick and County Tipperary
Murchadh O Briain made Earl of Thomond after the 1542 submission; the Composition of Thomond followed in 1585

capitals.name: Limerick
capitals.note: 'The O'Brien capital was located in Limerick' (Obrien supremacy section); no years.

capitals.name: Clonroad (Ennis)
capitals.note: Donnchadh 'moved his capital to Clonroad' in the Norman period; the year is not given.

correction.text: 'associated geographically with present-day County Clare as well as parts of County Limerick and County Tipperary'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has none. The page gives no area. Limerick city changed hands in the 1170s and was 'won back for Thomond' in 1369, so the Limerick part is soft; the page dates neither the Norman loss nor the lordship of the de Clares (ended at Dysert O'Dea, 1318).

ledger.note: 1118: Thomond is partitioned from Munster. 'In 1118 Conchobair partitioned Munster between the sons of Diarmait and Tagh Mac Carthaig.'
1174: the Dal gCais defeat a Norman army. 'The Dal gCais defeated a Norman army at the Battle of Thurles in 1174.' Strongbow had marched into Thomond that year (Norman invasion article).

1176: Domhnall Mor retakes Limerick. After Raymond le Gros captured it, Domhnall retook it 'the following year' and 'burned it rather than have it in foreign hands'; the page's year for the capture is not sure, so 1176 is a bridge.

region.text: Thomond, whose ruling O'Brien dynasty came under English rule

ledger.note: 1543: the kingdom ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1543'; 'Not until the 1540s did the ruling O'Brien dynasty come under English rule'; Murchadh was made Earl of Thomond after the 1542 Limerick parliament.

wars.name: Norman invasion of Thomond
wars.outcome: Thurles 1174, Limerick burned 1175 or 1176, Corcomroe 1317; 'The end of the de Clares and Norman territorial claims in Thomond came the following year at the Battle of Dysert O'Dea' (1318).
wars.note: The de Clare grant of Thomond is not dated on the page; the contest events cover only 1174-1176.

certainty.note: Only the county of Clare is firm; Limerick and Tipperary parts are soft.

sources.title: Norman invasion of Ireland
sources.note: Strongbow's march into Thomond in early 1174.

notes: The infobox gives 1543; the body says the earldom came with the submission of 1542. Thomond's 12th-century capital (Limerick) and the Norman lordship of the de Clares (1318) are only partly dated. The Composition of Thomond (1585) is on the page. The Norman contest of 1174-1176 is mirrored in the Lordship of Ireland dossier.
